item.title: Garment workers clash with police at Mirpur-10
item.description:
Garment workers clashed with police in the Mirpur 10 area of the capital.

The clashes began at around 11:15 am today, Sunday, and ended at around 11:45 am. Workers had been protesting since morning by blocking the road at Mirpur 10 intersection, demanding that their minimum monthly wage be raised to Tk 30,000.

According to eyewitnesses, police repeatedly asked the workers to clear the road. At one point, around 11:15 am, workers threw bricks and stones at the police. The police then began baton-charging them and chased them away. They also used water cannons, sound grenades and tear gas shells.

Garment workers block Mirpur-10 again, demanding Tk 30,000 minimum wage, metro station gates closed

The workers were dispersed as a result. They later regrouped and continued throwing bricks and stones at police from different directions. Clashes and chases between the two sides followed. The situation continued until around 11:45 am.

Garment workers had been protesting since morning by blocking the road at Mirpur 10 intersection in the capital, demanding that the minimum monthly wage be raised to Tk 30,000.

At around 8:00 am today, Sunday, workers from several garment factories blocked the road. This has disrupted traffic in the surrounding area.The gates of Mirpur 10 metro station were closed due to the blockade.

Gazipur garment workers block Dhaka–Tangail Highway, set police box on fire

Shortly before 11:00 am, Prothom Alo’s Administration Department official ABM Khairul Kabir, who was at the scene, said he had been unable to enter the station because its gates were closed. He later went to Kazipara station and boarded a metro train there.

Saiful Islam, a sub-inspector (SI) at Mirpur Police Station, told Prothom Alo that garment workers had gathered from several locations in Mirpur this morning and blocked Mirpur 10 intersection. Police have been sent to the scene, he said.

Garment workers had also blocked roads in Mirpur on Saturday over the same demand. The blockade brought traffic to a standstill in Mirpur 10, 11 and 12, as well as surrounding areas, from 10:30 am to 1:00 pm.

Workers clash with police repeatedly in Gazipur, 30 injured 15 vehicles vandalised

At one point, the workers gathered in the Shah Ali area of Mirpur 1. Several markets and garment factories were vandalised there.

There were also scuffles, chases and clashes between the workers and security personnel. In addition, workers threw bricks and stones at a garment factory in the Kalshi area.

Meanwhile, a wage board will be formed today to determine new wages for garment workers. Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury said this.

At a press briefing after a meeting at the Department of Labour headquarters in Bijoynagar area of the capital, on Saturday, the minister said there was no reason for workers to continue their protests in these circumstances.

item.title: Many entrepreneurs unable to get loans they need
item.description:
Hat Bakso, a small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) that manufactures souvenirs, applied to a private bank for a Tk 2 million cash credit (CC) loan to finance its business operations.

However, the bank is unwilling to lend more than Tk 400,000–500,000. Bank officials have assured the company that if it provides collateral, they can offer a loan worth up to 70–80 per cent of the value of its assets. Yet, just two and a half years ago, the company had received loans of the amount it needed from two banks and has been regularly paying interest on those loans.

Shafat Kadir, chief executive officer (CEO) of Hat Bakso, told Prothom Alo: “We are new entrepreneurs and do not have assets. However, we maintain regular daily transactions and pay the instalments on our existing loans on time. Even so, the bank is willing to provide only one-fourth of the amount we applied for. We cannot do anything with such a small amount. We also applied for a supply chain loan at another bank but have not received it in three months. How can we expand our business if we cannot get loans when we need them?”

Like Shafat Kadir, many businesspeople are unable to secure the loans they need from banks. Even large businesses are showing little interest in investment. Despite various government initiatives, closed industrial units have not resumed operations on any significant scale. As a result, the sluggish conditions that have gripped the private sector for several years are becoming even more pronounced.

Meanwhile, more than half of the country’s banks have largely withdrawn from industrial lending. Their boards of directors are unwilling to take on any new risks. Consequently, private sector credit growth has fallen to its lowest level in history. Credit growth in the private sector has remained below 5 per cent for six consecutive months. Yet, even with an average lending rate of 10 per cent, credit growth would normally be expected to be at a similar level.

In May, Bangladesh Bank announced a Tk 620 billion incentive package to revive activity in the financial sector. Of this amount, Tk 200 billion was allocated to reopening closed factories.

As of 15 October, Tk 5.61 billion had been disbursed from the fund earmarked for reopening closed factories. Meanwhile, approximately Tk 119.6 billion had been released from the entire Tk 620 billion package by the same date.

According to central bank data, private sector credit growth stood at 4.72 per cent in March. It remained at a similar level in April. In May, it edged up slightly to 4.98 per cent before declining again in June and July.

Credit growth stood at 4.75 per cent in August. As a result, private sector credit growth has remained below 5 per cent for six consecutive months. In the 2025–26 fiscal year, credit growth was 4.47 per cent.

Bank officials say businesses that have already invested are now facing uncertainty, leaving little momentum for new investment. Very little lending is going to the industrial sector.

A large share of the loans being disbursed is being used to finance imports of consumer goods and raw materials. Some consumer loans are also being issued. To increase credit growth, the private sector must regain momentum.

That would lead to an increase in lending. In the past, many loans were disbursed under fictitious names and were not put to much use in investment. This has contributed to the deterioration of the banking sector.

Businesses unable to secure loans

Members of the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA), including NH Apparels, Munshi Attires, DK Knitwear and Fatullah Fashion, have applied for loans from the incentive fund to reopen 78 closed factories.

Another 109 partially closed factories have also sought loans from the fund. However, the owners of these factories are not receiving much response.

On the matter, BKMEA President Mohammad Hatem told Prothom Alo: “As far as we know, no company in the knitwear sector has received a loan from the incentive fund so far. The boards of a few banks have approved loans for two to four partially operational factories, and the proposals have been sent to the central bank. However, no bank board has approved a loan for any closed factory.”

He added that the government wants to restore momentum to business and trade, and the central bank is sincere in its efforts. However, commercial banks are not coming forward adequately in this regard.

Hifs Agro Food Industries, based in Chattogram, applied to a private bank for a Tk 200 million cash credit loan. The bank offered to lend Tk 30–40 million. However, as that amount would not meet its needs, the company has shown little interest in pursuing the loan.

Syed Md Shoaib Hasan, CEO of Hifs Agro Food Industries, told Prothom Alo that no bank was currently willing to lend more than 70–80 per cent of the value of collateral. In the past, however, banks had provided loans worth 120 per cent or more of the collateral’s value.

“Our products used to take 45 days to reach various countries in the Middle East. Now it takes three months. As a result, we need more working capital than before. But we are not getting support from banks. Consequently, we are losing business opportunities,” he said.

Two companies under the steel-sector RRM Group have an approved credit limit of Tk 6 billion for their business operations. However, the group has sought an additional Tk 2 billion in credit facilities because of the rise in the dollar’s price, the reduction in letters of credit (LC) limits and an increase in other business costs. The bank is not approving the request.

Confirming the matter, RRM Group Chairman and Bangladesh Steel Manufacturers Association Secretary General Sumon Chowdhury told Prothom Alo that 48 companies control 90 per cent of the steel market. Of these, 30–32 companies have failed to secure requests for additional credit limits. Due to a shortage of funds, the companies are operating at half their production capacity. “If this continues, the industrial sector will not be able to recover,” he said.

Credit growth in the past

Private sector credit growth stood at 25.84 per cent in the 2010–11 fiscal year, before falling to 19.72 per cent in the following fiscal year. In the 2023–24 and 2024–25 fiscal years, credit growth was 9.84 per cent and 6.49 per cent, respectively.

An analysis of Bangladesh Bank data shows that credit growth accelerated before and after the national elections in 2014 and 2018.

New initiatives to revive the private sector

The government has taken new policy measures, alongside incentives, to increase the flow of credit to the private sector. To this end, Bangladesh Bank has reduced its policy rate for the first time in 21 months. The repo rate, or policy interest rate, has been lowered from 10 per cent to 9.5 per cent.

As a result, banks’ cost of borrowing from Bangladesh Bank has fallen somewhat, creating scope for lending rates to gradually decline. Relevant stakeholders believe, lower lending rates would help boost investment and employment.

However, entrepreneurs consider infrastructure-related issues, including gas and electricity supply, to be major obstacles. They also take the law and order situation into account. Long-standing problems such as tax policy, bribery and corruption remain as well.

Mohammad Ali, managing director of Pubali Bank, told Prothom Alo that many banks had reduced their lending activities after running into difficulties. Besides, there has been little new investment. However, he expects credit growth to gradually increase as disbursement under the incentive package gets underway.

Will the economy regain momentum?

On the one hand, Bangladesh Bank has taken steps to lower interest rates to stimulate the economy. On the other, it has lifted the lending limit imposed on state-owned Sonali Bank to increase loan disbursements. As a result, the bank will be able to lend as it sees fit in response to customer applications.

Since taking office, the BNP government has placed the highest priority on increasing investment and employment. In its election manifesto, the BNP set a target of turning Bangladesh into a trillion-dollar economy by 2034.

Reducing interest rates was also part of the discussion on investment-friendly policies to achieve this goal. Many sound entrepreneurs are now getting loans at interest rates below 10 per cent.

Abul Kasem Khan, former president of the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry and vice-chairman of A K Khan & Company, told Prothom Alo that the government measures to stimulate the economy were positive.

Many reforms had been undertaken, and more were underway, to improve the business environment. However, their impact would take time to materialise. The global situation was also not favourable, and business confidence had yet to recover.

Abul Kasem Khan added: “The business environment in Bangladesh has still not improved. It takes a year just to complete the procedures required to start a business. A task that should take one day ends up taking a year. Meanwhile, countries such as China and Thailand have moved far ahead. In this age of artificial intelligence, we need to rethink how to improve the business environment. We are encouraging solar power, but offering no incentives. Many countries are providing incentives for the use of solar power.”

item.title: Tenants leave government colonies as inspections set to begin
item.description:
“On 22 October, the landlord suddenly served me with a notice to vacate the flat. I was at my village home for the Durga Puja holidays at the time. When I returned to Dhaka on the 26th, I could not stay in the flat for even another day. I wandered from place to place, staying wherever I could. The landlord strictly instructed me to remove all my belongings and leave by 31 October.”

A third-year student at Eden Mohila College was describing her experience. She rented a room in a flat in a building at Azimpur Government Colony (Zone B) in the capital. She was one of many students living in the colony as subtenants.

The student was found at Azimpur Government Colony on Saturday at around 11:15 am. She was loading furniture and other belongings onto a van.

Requesting anonymity, the student said the agreement was that the landlord would give at least two months’ notice before asking her to leave.

Similarly, tenants were required to give two months’ notice if they wished to vacate the flat. However, neither condition was respected. Instead, she was forced to leave abruptly.

“We have our final examinations next December. I do not know how I will prepare for them in this situation. It will take me at least a month to recover from this trauma,” she said.

Students from various educational institutions, including the University of Dhaka, Eden Mohila College, Begum Badrunnesa Government Women's College, College of Applied Human Science (Home Economics College) and Dhaka College, rent rooms as subtenants at Azimpur Government Colony. Most of them are female students, who feel safe living in the government colony.

The students rent accommodation there out of necessity, as they come from different districts and securing a place in their respective institutions' halls of residence is not easy. The exact number of students living in the colony is unknown. However, students estimate that the figure could exceed 1,000.

Many government employees rent out their allotted flats. Some let out their entire flats, while others rent out one or two rooms.

Sources say a section of those who rent out their entire flats do so to live elsewhere at a lower cost while earning additional income from their government accommodation.

Another section has substantial additional income and no interest in living in their old government flats. They also want to earn extra money by renting out the properties. Those who rent out one or two rooms mainly do so because their salaries are insufficient to cover their living expenses.

This practice of renting out government accommodation has continued for years in Azimpur and other government colonies across Dhaka.

On Thursday, the Directorate of Government Accommodation, under the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, issued an urgent public notice stating that if any subtenant or tenant remained in a government flat after 31 October, the allotment of the flat to the relevant government employee would be cancelled. The notice also warned of disciplinary and legal action against those concerned.

A significant number of government employees at Azimpur Government Colony used to rent out their flats, while another section disapproved of the practice. Senior-ranking government officials, in particular, were opposed to it.

Speaking about the removal of tenants, Mahbub Alam, general secretary of the management committee of building no. 22 at Azimpur Government Colony (Zone B), told Prothom Alo that some residents might have rented out individual rooms, and complaints had been received about such cases.

“However, everyone has already been asked to leave. There are no tenants left,” he said.

Students said that, over the past few days, hundreds of students and tenants from other professions had been forced to leave their rented accommodation in the government colonies in Azimpur and Palashi.

However, many had yet to find new accommodation, as the search for a new home usually needs to begin at least a month in advance.

A third-year student at Begum Badrunnesa Government Women's College said, “I searched for accommodation in different areas every day until 11:00 pm or midnight. Even then, I could not find anywhere.”

She added, “We are renting accommodation in different places only because we could not secure a place in the halls of residence.”

The student urged the college authorities to arrange accommodation in the residential halls on an emergency basis in view of the situation.

A different picture in Paikpara, Tolarbag

The situation was different at the government officers' and employees' residential area in Paikpara, Mirpur-1. No one was seen leaving their accommodation during a visit to the area from 12:30 pm to 2:30 pm on Saturday.

Conversations with security guards at the colony gate and shopkeepers in the surrounding area yielded the same information. They also said they had not seen anyone leave their accommodation that day.

Meanwhile, several young men were seen in front of the old five-storey buildings at the Walk-up Government Employees' Residential Area in Mirpur-1.

They said the Public Works Department (PWD) had conducted raids on vacant flats and sealed them. Many residents of the area had already moved into the new multi-storey buildings nearby.

Inspections to be conducted

There are government colonies in various parts of the capital. According to statistics from the Directorate of Government Accommodation, the capital has a total of 19,091 government flats of different categories. Demand for rented accommodation is particularly high in the Azimpur area, which has 3,252 flats.

Meanwhile, Jahirul Islam Khan, director of the Directorate of Government Accommodation, told Prothom Alo that tenants and subtenants had been instructed to vacate their accommodation by 31 October.

Officials from the directorate would now conduct inspections. If they found anyone living in a flat as a subtenant or tenant, they would take legal action against the government employee in whose name the flat had been allotted.

Jahirul Islam said most tenants had already left their accommodation, while some were in the process of moving out.

He also said the authorities had not given tenants just one day's notice to vacate their flats. They had been given a week. Moreover, he questioned why people living there illegally should be given additional time, as they were occupying the accommodation unlawfully.

Students said everyone knew that people rented out flats at Azimpur Government Colony. They had no objection to the authorities asking tenants to leave. However, they said there was no need to subject people to unnecessary hardship.

Speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, a student said it was impossible to find accommodation within seven days. She had walked around helplessly searching for a place to stay but had found nothing.

“We are citizens of this country too. We have not committed any serious offence. What harm would it have caused the government if it had given us a month to find new accommodation and move out?” she said.

item.title: Gazipur garment workers block Dhaka–Tangail Highway, set police box on fire
item.description:
Garment workers have staged fresh protests in different areas of Gazipur, demanding that the minimum monthly wage be raised to Tk 30,000. Traffic on the Dhaka–Tangail Highway has been halted since Sunday morning due to the workers’ protests and blockades.

A police box in Konabari has been set on fire. Five platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed to keep the situation under control.

Workers took to the streets and began protesting this morning in Safipur Bazar, Chandra Palli Bidyut, Mouchak and Telichala areas of Kaliakair upazila in Gazipur. They chanted various slogans demanding higher wages.

Garment workers block Mirpur-10 again, demanding Tk 30,000 minimum wage, metro station gates closed

Kaliakair Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shahidul Islam said workers had been occupying the highway since this morning. As a result, traffic on the highway has come to a halt.

Gazipur Deputy Commissioner Md Nurul Karim Bhuiyan said five platoons of BGB personnel had been deployed in view of the current situation. The number of BGB personnel would be increased further if necessary, he added.

According to factory workers and police sources, garment workers have been protesting in different areas of Gazipur for nearly two weeks, demanding higher wages.

On Saturday, workers blocked the highway at Chandra Palli Bidyut and near Gate 3 of the Ansar Academy in Kaliakair until 8:30 pm. Police later dispersed them by charging batons and firing tear gas shells. Traffic on the highway returned to normal after about five hours.

This morning, workers from several factories, including Korani Knit Composite and Knit Asia in Ratanpur, Kaliakair, and nearby areas, did not report for work and took up positions on the highway in Safipur Bazar.

They began protesting after marking their attendance at the factories. Several nearby factories have declared holidays because of the workers’ movement.

Workers clash with police repeatedly in Gazipur, 30 injured 15 vehicles vandalised

Hundreds of workers later took up positions at various points along the highway, carrying sticks and poles. This brought traffic on the Dhaka–Tangail Highway to a complete standstill, leaving passengers travelling along the route in severe distress.

In the Konabari area of Gazipur city, protesting workers set fire to a police box located in the middle of the highway. They also took equipment and other belongings out of the police box and set those on fire, said Konabari Police Station OC Iftekhar Hossain.

item.title: HSC results re-scrutiny: Applications open, here’s how to apply
item.description:
The results of the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations were published yesterday, Saturday. Nearly 600,000 students have failed.

Many students may not have received the results they expected. Those who wish to do so can apply for re-scrutiny of their results.

The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee has also announced details of the application process and fee payment rules. Applications must be submitted online. No manual applications will be accepted.

Students dissatisfied with their published results can apply for re-scrutiny from today, Sunday (1 November 2026). The application process will continue until 7 November.

HSC: Exam dates for students who failed 1 or 2 subjects to be announced by 3 November

How to Apply for Result Re-scrutiny

Students must apply online through the designated website to have their results re-scrutinised. They need to visit the website and enter their roll and registration numbers in the designated fields. They must then select their education board from the dropdown list and click the ‘Submit’ button.

Students must then provide their mobile phone numbers. An SMS will be sent to those numbers when the re-scrutiny results are published.

The next screen will display the student’s subject-wise results. To request re-scrutiny of the results in one or more subjects, students must select the relevant subjects and click the ‘Pay Fee’ button.

The fee is Tk 150 per paper. For subjects with two papers, students must apply for both papers. The amount payable will be displayed in the next step. Fees can be paid through bKash, Nagad, DBBL Rocket, Upay and Sonali services. Detailed payment instructions can be found by clicking the ‘Pay’ button on the relevant portal.

More than half of male HSC candidates fail, female failure rate 43.69pc

After paying the fee, students must log in to the application portal and click the ‘Submit’ button. If they wish to add more subjects after submitting an application with a fee payment, they can do so by following the same procedure. However, they will not need to provide their mobile phone number again.

If students need to change or modify their applications before paying the fee, they can click the ‘Delete’ button to withdraw the selected subjects for which fees have not yet been paid. They can then select new subjects. However, once the fee has been paid, the subjects included in the application cannot be withdrawn. Under no circumstances will the fee be refunded.

item.title: Pakistan win tri-series: Zaman's century foils Sri Lanka
item.description:
CRICKET-PAK-SRI-ODI

Opener Fakhar Zaman returned to form with a brilliant century to help Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday.

Zaman, who overcame a wretched streak of just 31 runs in four matches, smashed a 99-ball 127 to help Pakistan chase down a target of 326 with nine balls to spare.

Sri Lanka pacer Dilshan Madushanka ended Zaman's innings in the 34th over with 106 needed for victory but Arafat Minhas (61) and Hasan Nawaz (37 not out) put on 94 for the sixth wicket to seal the win.

Minhas hit four sixes and three fours in his 31-ball innings.

Harmer, Rabada steer South Africa to series win over Australia

Skipper Shaheen Shah Afridi hit the winning six to send a packed Gaddafi Stadium into a frenzy.

This became Pakistan's first tri-series title at home after failing in the finals of the 1994, 2004 and 2025 tri-series.

Zaman, who cracked 11 fours and half a dozen sixes in his 12th ODI hundred, lifted Pakistan from a disastrous start after Maaz Sadaqat (5) and Babar Azam (0) fell with the total at 14.

Zaman added 149 off 140 balls for the third wicket with Saad Baig who scored a 74, bringing up his maiden ODI half-century.

Shaheen said he always believed in Zaman.

"We made a great comeback in bowling and then here was a collapse with the bat again, but Fakhar played a brilliant knock," said Shaheen of the opener who completed 4,000 ODI runs in his 97th match.

Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis blamed sloppy fielding.

"We were short of 25-30 runs but our bowling unit did well which was not supported by mistakes in the fielding," said Mendis referring to Zaman's drop catch on 69.

Earlier, Sri Lanka were lifted to 325-8 by Kamindu Mendis, who scored 131 for his maiden ODI century, after Pakistan won the toss and sent the tourists in to bat.

Kamindu and Pavan Rathnayake added 146 runs for the third wicket, before Pakistan skipper Shaheen dismissed Kamindu and Dasun Shanaka (17) in the space of two overs.

West Indies crush Bangladesh by eight wickets in Mirpur Test

Kamindu and Avishka Fernando (38) helped set Sri Lanka up for a big total as they shared an opening stand of 87 inside 18 overs.

Spinner Salman Agha, who took 2-44, provided Pakistan with a double breakthrough, getting rid of Fernando and Kusal Mendis (8).

But Kamindu anchored the innings, hitting 12 fours and two sixes, improving on his previous highest ODI score of 64.

Pakistan pulled it back in the last five overs, taking three wickets for just 38 runs to stop Sri Lanka from posting a larger total.

Shaheen finished with 2-50 while Haris Rauf and Naseem Shah also took two wickets each.

item.title: Movement will intensify until referendum verdict is implemented
item.description:
Shafiqur Rahman, leader of the opposition in parliament and ameer of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, has warned that the movement will be intensified if the referendum verdict is not implemented.

He said the movement would continue until the verdict was implemented, with each successive programme becoming stronger than the previous one.

Shafiqur made the remarks on Saturday during a long march by the 11-party alliance from Dhaka towards Khulna and Kushtia.

The long march began in the morning after a rally at the south gate of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque in the capital. Along the route, rallies were held at Naodoba in Shariatpur, Katakhali in Bagerhat, Babri Chattar and Swadhinata Chattar in Fultala in Khulna, and Murali intersection in Jashore.

At the time of writing this report at 9:00pm, a rally by the alliance was underway near the Jhenaidah-Chuadanga bus stand. The long march was scheduled to conclude with a rally in Kushtia later that night.

Thousands of people attended the roadside rallies, where Shafiqur and other senior leaders of the 11 parties addressed the crowds. The Jamaat chief also delivered brief speeches while standing in his vehicle at Hasnabad in South Keraniganj of Dhaka, Louhajang in Munshiganj, Kashiani in Gopalganj and Nawapara in Jashore.

Speaking at a rally at Babri Chattar, also known as Shibbari intersection, in Khulna in the afternoon, Shafiqur said they would not compromise with anyone and would return home only after securing their demands.

Earlier, speaking at a rally at Swadhinata Chattar in Fultala, the Jamaat chief said the alliance's seven-point demand could turn into a single-point demand at any time.

Addressing party activists, he said they might be called upon to travel to Dhaka for a one-point movement. A call might also come to take control of the streets across the country in a revolutionary movement, he added, urging everyone to remain prepared.

During the two previous long marches, National Citizen Party (NCP) convener Nahid Islam and member secretary Akhtar Hossain attended the opening rallies and joined the motorcades. Neither was seen in the motorcade or at the rallies this time. No NCP representative attended the rally in Dhaka in particular.

However, at least four central leaders of the party joined the motorcade, and some addressed the roadside rallies.

Sources within the NCP said that although the party remains part of the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, it wants to preserve its distinct identity as an independent political party. As part of that effort, the NCP held a mass protest at Shahbagh in Dhaka on Friday, a day before the alliance''s long march towards Khulna.

Demands must be met before the next parliamentary session

Speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural rally in Dhaka on Saturday morning, Shafiqur Rahman said the government must announce its decision to implement the referendum verdict before the next session of parliament begins on 9 November.

He said implementation of the referendum verdict was the principal demand among the alliance's seven points. The other six demands had arisen because the verdict had not been implemented, he added.

He also accused the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of breaking its promise to the nation and mocking the people's verdict.

Warning that the ruling BNP would have to pay a heavy price if it failed to implement the referendum verdict, the Jamaat chief said another inevitable revolution was knocking at the door and the people must be prepared for it.

Shafiqur also questioned whether the government was keeping the public in the dark over the Matarbari deep-sea port project.

He said the government must explain to the nation the purpose of the prime minister's recent visit to Japan and what had been achieved during the trip. In particular, the public wanted clarity on whether anything was being concealed regarding the Matarbari deep-sea port, he said.

"Bangladesh must not be leased out to anyone in the name of connectivity," he added.

The opposition leader further said, "Those who accepted subservience in the past are now facing the consequences. They had their ''elder sister'' and ''elder brother'' to turn to, but who do you have? You will not escape accountability for deceiving the people."

Addressing the rally, Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) president Colonel (retd) Oli Ahmed alleged that district councils, city corporations, municipalities and other public offices had been turned into BNP offices.

He accused the ruling party of controlling government tenders and seizing people's homesteads through these institutions. The prime minister needed to understand that, ultimately, all the blame would fall on his shoulders, he said.

People know how to secure their demands

Addressing a rally at Katakhali intersection in Bagerhat, the Jamaat chief said the BNP itself must implement the referendum verdict.

"Accept it peacefully. Otherwise, the people of this country know how to secure their demands," he said.

Bangladesh Khelafat Majlish ameer Maulana Mamunul Haque said the government was still in power because the opposition was cooperating with it. If the government refused to abandon its stubborn stance, the 11-party alliance would be compelled to take action, he warned.

NCP joint convener Abdul Hannan Masud said the government would not be able to remain in power unless it stopped terrorism and extortion and reduced gas and electricity prices.

Traffic congestion causes public suffering

According to data from the Padma Bridge toll plaza, the long-march convoy included microbuses, cars, jeeps and other vehicles. A total of 778 vehicles crossed the bridge.

Reports from Prothom Alo correspondents in the areas along the route said leaders and activists of the 11-party alliance gathered at several points along the Dhaka-Khulna highway for the roadside rallies. In some places, they stood on both sides of the road to welcome the leaders, who waved back at them.

The gatherings caused traffic congestion at several points along the highway.

Prothom Alo's Faridpur correspondent reported that severe traffic congestion developed when the long-march convoy left the Bhanga municipal office and headed towards Khulna. After crossing the Dhaka-Bhanga Expressway, vehicles had to slow down because of the congestion.

Other participants in the long march included Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar and Assistant Secretary General Hamidur Rahman Azad; NCP senior joint convener Hasnat Abdullah and joint convener Ariful Islam Adeeb; Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party acting ameer Abdul Qayyum Subhani; AB Party chairman Mujibur Rahman Manju; Labour Party chairman Mostafizur Rahman; and JAGPA vice-president Rashed Pradhan, among others.

The opposition alliance has seven demands: implementation of the referendum verdict; trial of the July massacre; resolution of shortages of electricity, fuel oil, gas and fertiliser; prevention of price hikes in essential commodities; improvement of the law and order situation; an end to corruption, extortion and land grabbing; and an end to narrow partisan control of institutions.

The 11-party alliance previously organised long marches towards Chattogram on 5 September and Rangpur on 19 September. The opposition alliance plans to hold another long march towards Sylhet on 21 November, followed by a grand rally in Dhaka.

item.title: FBI says North Korea behind USD 6b crypto theft from Binance
item.description:
FILES-US-CRYPTOCURRENCY-BITCOIN

The FBI on Saturday accused North Korea of stealing more than $6 billion in virtual assets from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance in what is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist.

The US law enforcement agency’s statement came as Binance offered reassurances it was covering the losses from the hacking attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90 per cent of what was stolen.

Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the cyberattack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday.

The FBI confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.

TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year.

“The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about 29 October, 2026,” the statement said.

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralized finance and instant swap services.

It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets.”

US President Donald Trump, however, cast doubt on the North Korea’s involvement in the hack.

“I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida late Saturday.

The president often reflects with pride on summits he held with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his first term.

‘Cover the financial impact’

Binance said Saturday it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack.

“Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X.

It said it has used company money to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of the stolen funds, while the remaining 10 per cent of tokens are “less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts.”

Binance suspended user withdrawals after the hack, but said in its latest update they were on track to resume Sunday.

The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

Bitcoin plunged nearly five percent after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly six percent and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10 percent.

Binance said Friday it was working to resolve what it called a “complex attack” with several “points of breach.”

The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea—which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programs—to find illicit means to capture revenue.

TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for “The Interview,” a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim.

item.title: 'My son was trained in swimming; he could not have drowned': Tahsif's father
item.description:
Former Bangladesh Air Force officer KM Tahsif Souri  was a trained swimmer. His father, AKM Eneyetul Karim, therefore believes that the young man could not have died by drowning.

Speaking to Prothom Alo today, Saturday, he said, “Why would he run away from someone chasing him? And who would chase him in the first place? That makes no sense. Nor would he have run away even if someone had chased him.”

Tahsif, a former flight lieutenant in the Bangladesh Air Force, left home last Tuesday after a friend called him but never returned. The following day, his body was recovered from the Turag River in Rajbari Ghat, an area in Dhaka’s Uttarkhan.

After 1:00am on Friday night, Tahsif’s father, K M Eneyetul Karim, filed a murder case with Uttarkhan police station against unidentified persons. The complaint alleges that Tahsif was murdered and his body dumped in the river to conceal the crime.

Before Tahsif went missing, CCTV footage showed him with another man. Family members identified the man as Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip, whom they described as a ‘younger friend’ of Tahsif.

The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) initially took Dwip into custody on Thursday. Today, the River Police formally arrested him. After a hearing, a Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) court granted police four days of remand for questioning.

Police said Dwip and Tahsif were together on the day of the incident. Based on information provided by Dwip, police recovered a motorcycle from the Mazar Basti area of Tongi. They suspect it belonged to Tahsif.

Father wants to know why his son died

Tahsif’s father, Eneyetul Karim, told Prothom Alo, “We want to know the cause of his death. We hope a proper investigation will establish what happened and ensure justice.”

Eneyetul Karim said he could not accept that his son had drowned. He reiterated that Tahsif had received swimming training.

According to his father, Tahsif was exceptionally brave and intelligent. He does not believe that his son would have run away after being chased by a police officer. He finds this absurd.

“Even if 100 police officers stood in front of a commissioned officer, he would not be expected to run away. GD pilots are among the best commissioned officers. The best candidates are selected to become GD pilots,” Eneyetul Karim said.

He said Tahsif left home shortly after 6:30pm on Tuesday. When Dwip called him from downstairs, Tahsif told his mother, “Mum, I’m just going out to have a quick word with him.”

He never returned home.

Eneyetul Karim said Tahsif’s mother repeatedly called to ask when he would return. Each time, he replied, “Mum, I’m coming, I’m coming.”

At 1:35am, Tahsif sent a voice message via Messenger saying that he was on his way. However, he did not say where he was leaving from. The family could not contact him after that. They called him throughout the night but received no response.

Just before the evening of the following day, River Police called to inform the family that Tahsif’s body had been found.

“We rushed there after receiving the news, but we could not collect the body that day. It had been sent to the morgue at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College for an autopsy. The body was handed over to me around noon on Thursday,” his father said.

‘I am extremely upset’

Tahsif’s death has left his father emotionally devastated. Referring to the online trolling directed at him on social media, Eneyetul Karim said, “I am extremely upset. As a father, I have lost my son. On top of that, people are trolling me on Facebook and elsewhere.

“I am the eldest of 11 siblings. My mother is a proud mother who is a ‘Ratna garbha’. I raised each of my brothers and sisters to become someone they could be proud of. I built this large family. Because of that, I have to remain strong.”

He said breaking down and crying in front of journalists would not bring his son back.

“When an accident happens, I try to make things easier for everyone around me so that they can find the mental courage and strength to cope. What is happening inside me, how I am breaking down, how I am crying uncontrollably and screaming—that happens inside my room or in the bathroom. I see it, and Allah sees it. Whatever happens, it is a personal matter,” Eneyetul Karim said.

Questions over Dwip’s account

Tahsif’s father said the family had contacted his son’s friend, Dwip. Dwip told him that they had dinner together and that he had dropped Tahsif off near his home before leaving. However, Tahsif’s motorcycle was later found some distance away.

Eneyetul Karim questioned the account: “If Dwip had left Tahsif near his home, how did the motorcycle end up being found there?”

He added, “When I could not find my son, I asked his friend specifically where they had parted ways. He said they had said goodbye outside Gate No. 1. Then he said they had parted inside the gate.

“He also told me that he had returned home by midnight. Later, I learned that he had returned home after 2:30am. These things raise questions.”

Tahsif’s father further said Dwip had told police that the two had gone towards Rajbari Ghat. There, they allegedly saw two people wearing police uniforms and ran away. Another account later claimed that Tahsif had jumped into the river. His father said he did not personally know what had happened.

“I know nothing about this. However, Dwip told me that he had left my son there. Later, I heard that his motorcycle had been found at that location. If they went there together, the inconsistencies in these accounts naturally raise questions,” Eneyetul Karim said.

He said he did not know what had happened after his son left home but believed the circumstances were highly unusual.

“This is something I cannot accept in the case of my son,” he said.

Tahsif had worked at the Bangladesh Cricket Board and later at Netra News. His father has called for a fair investigation to establish the actual cause of his son’s death.

HRSS calls for impartial investigation

The Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) has expressed deep concern and grief over the mysterious death of K M Tahsif Souri . The organisation has called for an independent, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the actual cause of death.

In a statement issued today, HRSS said there were inconsistencies in the information and accounts surrounding Tahsif’s death. These needed to be verified through an impartial investigation, it said.

The organisation called for the publication of the autopsy and chemical examination reports, the preservation of digital and physical evidence, the protection of family members and witnesses, and safeguards for the legal rights of the person in custody.

Political participation becoming a ‘power-centric business model’: Iftekharuzzaman
item.description:
Abuse of power, black money and the criminalisation of politics are fuelling internal conflicts within major political parties, remarked Iftekharuzzaman, executive director of Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB).

As a result, he said, political participation or party affiliation is in many cases turning into a “power-centric business model”.

Iftekharuzzaman made the remarks at a press conference at TIB’s office in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, on Sunday afternoon. The event was organised to launch a research report titled Institutional Good Governance in Bangladesh’s Political Parties.

Responding to a question, Iftekharuzzaman said the July uprising had raised expectations that the practice of power politics would come to an end. In reality, however, nothing had changed.

According to him, power politics was fuelling factionalism and internal conflicts within parties, with people even losing their lives as a result. The problem was becoming more pronounced at the local level than at the national level, he said, describing the situation as worrying.

Highlighting the lack of good governance in the internal affairs of political parties, the TIB executive director said the absence of effective safeguards against irregularities, corruption and abuse of power, coupled with a lack of accountability, had led to the use of money and muscle power within major political parties. As a result, political violence was becoming normalised.

Iftekharuzzaman also spoke about political party financing. He said the prevailing political culture required substantial sums of money to run party activities. The funds were managed through informal processes, which were largely dependent on individuals, inevitably resulting in a lack of transparency.

There was also a substantial discrepancy between parties’ officially reported income and expenditure and the actual figures, he said.

He said there were serious shortcomings in good governance across virtually every aspect of the internal and institutional functioning of political parties.

He pointed out that despite the existence of laws and regulations, the legal framework remained inadequate to ensure internal democratic practices and transparency and accountability in political financing.

There were also inconsistencies between the country’s legal framework and international legal practices, Iftekharuzzaman added.

Pointing to discrepancies between Bangladesh’s party registration practices and those of other countries, the TIB executive director said the process was excessively restrictive in many cases.

At the same time, he said, the absence of effective mechanisms to ensure transparency and accountability meant that a system based on legal requirements could, from the outset, foster money-driven competition for patronage.

Iftekharuzzaman also highlighted the dominance of dynastic and elitist tendencies in party leadership.

Responding to a question, he said inadequate participation by grassroots representatives, people from diverse backgrounds and women was allowing dynastic and elite interests to dominate leadership development.

Meanwhile, ordinary people with the ability to lead at the local level were being denied opportunities, he said. “This can never be positive for democratic practice. The situation needs to change.”

The TIB executive director stressed the importance of internal reforms to ensure institutional good governance within political parties.

He said internal reform was essential to ensuring good governance in the institutional functioning of political parties, which are among the major institutions of democracy.

Responsibility for reform rests with the political parties themselves, Iftekharuzzaman said. As a prerequisite for the future of democracy in the country and for restoring public trust in political parties, their leaders must hold themselves to account and take reform proposals seriously, he added.

The research report was presented at the press conference by TIB senior research fellow Mohammad Zulkarnain, research associates Kawsar Ahmed and Kazi Aminul Hasan.

Also present were TIB adviser-executive management Professor Sumaiya Khair, director of the Research and Policy Division Mohammad Badiuzzaman, and director of the Outreach and Communication Division Mohammad Touhidul Islam.

item.title: Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail: Rahul Gandhi
item.description:
ANI_20261101323

Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Sunday said that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be removed from his post and jailed, while accusing him of facilitating alleged vote theft in the country.

Addressing the INDIA bloc’s mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in the national capital, Rahul Gandhi asserted that action would be taken against the CEC and claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah would not have reached their respective positions without him.

“Listen to me. What I say always turns out to be true, doesn’t it? I am telling every citizen and every youth of India: Gyanesh Kumar will be removed from the post of chief election commissioner. Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail. Without Gyanesh Kumar, neither Narendra Modi would have become prime minister nor Amit Shah would have become home minister,” he said.

Rahul Gandhi also raised concerns over issues facing farmers, youth and labourers, alleging that they were being denied their rights and that the country’s wealth was concentrated in the hands of a few people.

“The farmer is not getting his rights. The youth are not getting employment. The labourer is not getting his rights, and the entire wealth has gone into the hands of two or three people. We do not want such an India, and we will not accept such an India,” he added.

The Congress leader also alleged that vote theft had taken place in several Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, claiming that votes were manipulated through Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and changes to electoral rolls.

“For years, vote theft has been happening in this country. Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections: in all these elections, vote theft has occurred. Votes have been stolen through EVMs and by deleting and adding names to voter lists,” he said.

Rahul Gandhi further claimed that 15 per cent of India’s voters were removed from electoral rolls after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, describing the election as illegal and stolen.

“It was a stolen election. I am not the one saying this; the election commission is saying this,” he said.

INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, attended the rally organised against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Top Opposition leaders and supporters from across the country gathered at the venue for the INDIA bloc’s “Chalo Delhi” protest march, raising concerns over the SIR exercise and alleged irregularities in electoral rolls.

The march began from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction and proceeded towards Ramlila Maidan. The gathering followed a public “impeachment” programme against the CEC held in the national capital on 31 October.

“Democracy will survive if PM Modi goes”

Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the BJP-led governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh of coming to power through what he termed “vote theft”, and called for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ouster from office.

Addressing the INDIA bloc’s mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in the national capital, Kharge alleged that those in power were choosing themselves rather than being elected by the public.

“Who votes for them? They choose themselves. The public does not elect them. The current central government, as well as the governments in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, are all governments of vote theft. We must remove these thieves,” Kharge said.

“Only if Modi goes will democracy survive. We must remove Modi to save democracy,” he added.

Meanwhile, BJP leader and Sambalpur MP Dharmendra Pradhan participated in the party’s ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ (Save Democracy, End Anarchy) padayatra in Faridabad on Sunday, where he accused Rahul Gandhi and the Congress of losing faith in democratic institutions.

Pradhan was accompanied by Union Minister of State Krishan Pal Gurjar, Minister of State Rajesh Nagar, Haryana Sports Minister Gaurav Gautam, several MLAs and party workers during the march, organised as part of the BJP’s nationwide campaign.

Shashi Tharoor demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, Surjewala calls protest ‘people’s revolution’

During the Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan rally, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign, saying that people had lost faith in him.

Speaking to ANI, Tharoor said, “It looks like the voice of the people has been aroused, and it is time for Gyanesh Kumar to hear the voice of the people. If he has got an ounce of moral conscience, he should see that people have lost faith in him and he should quit.”

Congress MP Randeep Surjewala described the gathering as the beginning of a people’s revolution and accused the government of attacking the Constitution and allowing alleged electoral irregularities.

He added that the message raised at Ramlila Maidan under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders would resonate across the country.

“A people’s revolution has begun in the country. The throne of the ‘emperor’ is shaking, and the people of this nation are sending a clear message: neither will attacks on the Constitution be tolerated, nor will the theft of votes. This clarion call—raised from Ramlila Maidan under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and the entire opposition—will resonate across every corner of the country,” Surjewala said.

Congress leader Kumari Selja claimed that hundreds of thousands of people had assembled at the venue to oppose the BJP government and the functioning of the chief election commissioner.

She said the INDIA bloc leaders and supporters had taken a pledge not to allow the prevailing situation to continue and asserted that the people had made their decision to bring down the government.

“A massive sea of hundreds of thousands of people has gathered today at the Ramlila Maidan. Under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi, the entire INDIA bloc—all its leaders and hundreds of thousands of supporters—have taken a solemn pledge today: we will not allow the state of affairs that the BJP and the chief election commissioner have brought about in this country to continue. We will topple this government; the people have made their decision,” she said.

Senior Advocate and Congress MP Abhishek Manu Singhvi said the rally conveyed a message of public anger and discontent.

“This is a message. A message of outrage, of discontent. It is a message that the Constitution is not anyone’s plaything,” Singhvi said.

“West Bengal is victim of SIR”: Mamata Banerjee vows to continue fight at INDIA bloc rally

Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee today said that people in Bengal are “victims” of the SIR and vowed to continue the fight against the exercise, asserting that she would not surrender.

Addressing the INDIA bloc’s mega rally, Banerjee accused the BJP of looting West Bengal and said the fight to protect democracy would continue through political and democratic means.

“Bengal is the victim of the circumstances of this SIR. We will not give up. We will give our lives, we will fight, but we will not surrender. They looted our Bengal. We will save democracy and bring it back. We will take revenge through politics. We will take revenge through democracy. We will fight,” she said.

Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav targeted the BJP and asserted that the party and its allies would not return to power after the 2027 Assembly elections.

“Those who once came from UP will be driven out from UP itself. The people of UP know how to welcome and how to bid farewell even better. In 2027, such a farewell will happen that the Bharatiya Janata Party and its allies will not be able to return again,” Yadav said.

Describing the gathering at Ramlila Maidan as the “Haldighati of democracy”, the SP chief said the public support and slogans at the rally reflected the possibility of change.

“Today, Ramlila Maidan has turned into the Haldighati of democracy. The massive public support and slogans of revolution are proof that change can happen at any moment,” Yadav said.

Taking dig at the BJP, he said those who had earlier claimed to be an “unmovable foot of Angad” had lost their political ground. Referring to Kashi, he said the people there had given the party a “double zero”.

“Those who claimed to be an ‘unmovable foot of Angad’ now have no ground left beneath them. The people of Kashi have given them a double zero,” Yadav said.

Yadav also alleged that the BJP was conspiring because it could not win public support and accused the party of using the Election Commission to pursue its political objectives.

“You and I have seen that the BJP is continuously plotting conspiracies because they know they cannot win among the public. So they have chosen their path through the Election Commission,” he added.

“Assassinated Constitution, assassinated Sikhs, now assassinating democracy”: Anurag Thakur slams Congress over Delhi protest

Bhartiya Janta Party (BJP) MP Anurag Thakur has strongly criticised the Congress and opposition parties over their protests in the national capital, accusing them of attempting to create political instability and spread anarchy in the country.

He asserted that India’s democratic institutions remain strong and that the people would never allow the country to become like Bangladesh, Nepal, Libya or Syria.

Thakur highlighted India’s economic progress under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, stating that the country had become the world’s fourth-largest economy and would continue to advance in the coming years.

“They assassinated the Constitution, assassinated Sikhs, and now they have set out to assassinate democracy and spread anarchy. But the people of the country will never let India become Bangladesh, Nepal, Libya, or Syria. India’s democracy is strong, and under Modi ji’s leadership, India has become the fourth-largest economy in the world, and will move forward even more now,” he said.

Commenting on the protests in Delhi, Thakur referred to the gathering outside Himachal Bhawan, where protesters had assembled and raised slogans. He questioned the performance of the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh, alleging that it had failed to fulfil its electoral guarantees and was now organising protests in the national capital to avoid accountability for its governance.

“The Congress government in Himachal Pradesh has failed to deliver anything, and its guarantees have fallen flat. Now, to avoid being held accountable here, they have gone to Delhi. They should ask what happened to Priyanka Gandhi’s guarantees and Rahul Gandhi’s guarantees. This political drama by the Congress is not acceptable to the people of the country.” he said.

When asked about allegations of a foreign toolkit being used against the government, Thakur maintained that the opposition could not challenge the government through its own strength.

“Foreign toolkit, foreign money, foreign forces, foreign friends. The opposition would never dare to think about toppling the government in India using their strength,” he said.

Thakur dismissed the opposition’s demonstration as political drama, asserting that it would not yield any results.

“It’s just drama from Congress and the opposition; nothing is going to come of it. Nothing will happen. The people of this country are watching,” he said.

Responding to questions concerning allegations of voter deletions from electoral rolls, Thakur defended the removal of ineligible entries.

“If a dead person’s vote was deleted, then a dead person’s vote should be deleted. If someone has moved, their vote should be deleted; duplicate votes should be deleted. The vote of someone who isn’t present at home should be deleted, and that’s exactly what’s happening. If 13 crore people’s votes had been deleted, there would have been a massive uproar in India, brother, but that’s not the case,” he stated.

“Get ready to spend another 5 years in opposition”: Amit Shah

Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched a blistering, no-holds-barred counter-offensive against the INDIA Bloc’s mega rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan.

Shah mounted a fierce attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and the INDIA bloc, warning them that their politics of “obstruction and negativity” would ensure they remain permanently banished from power.

Ridiculing the opposition alliance’s playbook, Shah asserted that disrupting legislative proceedings and staging street drama will only push them further into political irrelevance.

“Lying, spreading chaos, propagating negativity, obstructing the functioning of Parliament, and taking parliamentary issues to the streets to create a ruckus—if this has been your nature, then get ready to spend another five years in the opposition,” he said.

Tearing into Rahul Gandhi over his political ambitions, Shah took a sharp dig at Sonia Gandhi, stating that her political dream would remain unfulfilled.

“For 15 years—effectively spanning three elections—he has been losing. Sonia-ji’s dream of seeing her son become prime minister remains unfulfilled. She has come up with a new approach: holding a ‘mock parliament’. I would like to tell Rahul-ji: if you want to be prime minister, then just stay in a ‘mock parliament’ for the rest of your life—because your turn is never going to come.” Shah said.

Shah added, “...Rahul ji, you disrupt the functioning of Parliament—all to prevent mothers and sisters from securing 33 per cent reservation. Rahul Baba, let me tell you this: it is this very Narendra Modi ji who will ensure that the women of India—our ‘Matrushakti’—receive 33 per cent reservation; this is our firm resolve”

The union home minister also flagged the timing of the rally, pointing out how the opposition turned a blind eye to both the business community ahead of the festive season and the historic sensitivity surrounding the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

“Traders in Delhi pleaded with them, explaining that they have only one week in the entire year when the bulk of their business takes place. ‘If we stock up on sweets and they don’t sell, what happens? We suffer a loss. If we stock up on firecrackers and they don’t sell, what happens? We suffer a loss...’” Shah noted.

“The traders held press conferences—not once, but three times—wrote letters, and implored them to hold their rally after Diwali. But no—they insisted on holding their rally on that very day—the same dark day when the anti-Sikh riots, the Sikh massacre, took place,” the home minister remarked.

Issuing a stern electoral prediction, Amit Shah warned the Congress that Delhi’s trading fraternity would deliver a decisive blow at the ballot box.

“I want to tell the leaders of the Congress party today: the small traders of Delhi have ensured that you haven’t been able to open an account—that is, win a single seat—in the last three elections. And mark my words: you won’t be able to open an account in the next three elections either,” Shah declared.

Setting a firm deadline to eliminate the narcotics crisis, Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared that the central government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi will make the entire country, including Punjab, completely free from the menace of drugs by 31 December 2029.

“On one hand, Narendra Modi-ji is propelling the nation forward at an extraordinary pace. Article 370 has been abolished; Naxalism has been brought to an end; ‘Triple Talaq’ has been abolished,” he said.

“Now, mark my words: by 31 December 2029, we will ensure that the entire country—including Punjab—is completely free from the menace of drugs,” Shah asserted.
