item.title: Govt steps up efforts to prevent sabotage amid labour unrest
item.description:
The government has stepped up efforts to control the situation in industrial areas following protests, road blockades and clashes between readymade garment workers and police over their demand for a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Alongside forming a new wage board to determine the minimum wage for garment workers, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a meeting with relevant ministers and advisers to review the overall situation. Law enforcement agencies have also arrested several people over allegations of vandalism, arson and involvement in sabotage.
The meeting, chaired by Tarique Rahman, was held at the Cabinet Division conference room at the secretariat on Sunday evening.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, PM’s adviser and also PMO Spokesperson Mahdi Amin and Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal chief coordinator and transport leader Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas attended the meeting.
Earlier in the morning, Labour Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced the formation of a new six-member wage board to determine the minimum wage for garment workers. He said forming the wage board had been a key demand of the workers and urged those protesting to leave the streets and return to their workplaces following the government's decision.
The government has formed a new wage board to determine the minimum wage for garment workers, incorporating representatives from both employers and workers, along with an independent member.
Senior District and Sessions Judge Sheikh Ashfakur Rahman has been appointed chairman of the board.
The labour minister said the government expected the board members to hold discussions promptly and take steps to determine a wage structure that would be acceptable to workers.
However, the date of the board's first meeting and the deadline for announcing the new wage structure have yet to be determined.
Despite the government's announcement of the new wage board, protests and road blockades continued on Sunday in Mirpur in the capital, Kaliakair in Gazipur, and the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt. Clashes with police, vandalism and arson were reported at several locations.
Garment workers began protesting from the Mirpur-10 roundabout in the morning, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. The demonstrations later spread to Mirpur-11, Mirpur-12 and surrounding areas.
Clashes between workers and police broke out at around 11:30am and continued until the afternoon.
Vehicular movement came to a halt on several roads in Mirpur. As tensions escalated, the Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11 and Pallabi metro rail stations were temporarily closed. At one point, a police vehicle beneath the Mirpur-11 metro station was set on fire.
In Gazipur's Kaliakair Upazila, workers staged demonstrations in Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Safipur, Mouchak and Konabari.
The blockade of the Dhaka-Tangail Highway disrupted traffic for nearly six hours. A garment factory warehouse and a vehicle belonging to law enforcement agencies were reportedly set on fire during the unrest.
Police fired tear gas and sound grenades to bring the situation under control. Traffic gradually began to return to normal after workers left the roads.
Protests in various parts of Savar and Ashulia also disrupted traffic on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway, particularly around Hemayetpur and several other locations.
According to industrial police, 177 factories in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt and more than 100 factories in Gazipur declared a holiday for Sunday amid the unrest. Production was suspended at more than 300 factories in total.
Police have arrested several people in Mirpur and Gazipur over allegations of vandalism, arson and sabotage during the workers' protests.
The Mirpur division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police said 29 people had been arrested in connection with Sunday's demonstrations in the area. Industrial police, meanwhile, reported the arrest of 20 people in the Gazipur industrial zone.
Police also said they had arrested nine activists and leaders of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations during operations in different parts of Kaliakair Upazila in Gazipur.
According to police, those arrested include individuals affiliated with the Awami League, Jubo League, Chhatra League, Krishak League and Sramik League at various levels.
Kaliakair Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shahidul Islam said the arrests were made following allegations that the individuals were involved in various criminal activities.
Police have also alleged political involvement in the labour unrest. However, the specific allegations against those arrested, details of the cases filed and whether the charges can be established in court will be determined through the judicial process.
Labour Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury has alleged that some political organisations are deliberately attempting to create instability in the garment industry.
He claimed that outsiders had thrown stones at several factories and attempted to mobilise workers to take to the streets.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Rashed Khan, a political assistant to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, alleged in a social media post that a Chhatra League leader had been leading a workers' protest in Gazipur. He also questioned the role of various political groups in the unrest.
Following the formation of the wage board, the labour minister urged protesting workers to return to their workplaces. The government has assured them that the process of determining the minimum wage will move forward through discussions.
It remains unclear what recommendations the new board will make.

item.title: Heat costs Bangladesh $17.5bn in potential earnings
item.description:
Climate change is taking an increasing toll on Bangladesh’s health and economy, with heat exposure alone causing an estimated loss of $17.5 billion in potential earnings in 2025, according to the 2026 Lancet Countdown Report on Health and Climate Change.
Heatwave exposure among infants and older people has more than doubled compared with 1986–2005, while human-caused fine particulate air pollution was responsible for an estimated 239,000 deaths in 2023.
The report highlights growing threats to health and livelihoods in Bangladesh as the report’s authors call for climate change to be formally recognised and addressed as a global health emergency, urging governments to place health at the centre of climate decisions, from emissions reduction targets to funding priorities.
The tenth annual report on Lancet Countdown, subtitled A decade of escalating health harms and a decisive moment for all, finds that many climate-related health risks and harms grew faster during 2016-2025 than during the preceding decade.
The Bangladesh findings were presented at a national launch at Brac Centre Inn in Dhaka on Sunday, organised by the Centre for Climate Change and Environmental Research (C3ER), Brac University, with technical support from the Climate Change and Health Promotion Unit (CCHPU), Health Services Division, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. Shouro Dasgupta delivered the keynote presentation.
The event was moderated by Dr Iqbal Kabir, coordinator of the Climate Change and Health Promotion Unit (CCHPU) of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Md Golam Rabbani, director, C3ER, Brac University, provided his welcome remarks.
He stated that over the past two decades, we have discussed climate change largely through disasters such as cyclones, storm surges and salinity intrusion. But their consequences for people’s health have often received less attention.
“Bangladesh’s climate policies recognise health as a priority alongside agriculture and water. Yet implementation has not received the attention and resources it needs.”
“The urgency is clear. Heat stress is affecting farmers, outdoor workers and urban communities, while dengue has become a recurring public health concern. These risks affect people’s health, livelihoods and ability to work safely.”
“Today’s report brings evidence to help us respond. We must use it to strengthen prevention, early warning and health-system preparedness, and turn our policy commitments into practical action.”
Dr Shouro Dasgupta, environmental economist, Fondazione CMCC and visiting senior fellow, Grantham Research, delivered the keynote presentation.
Bangladesh lost an average of more than 26 billion potential labour hours annually between 2016 and 2025 because of heat exposure, 71% higher than the annual average in the 1990s, he added.
According to the report, during 2021–2025, infants and people aged over 65 experienced an average of 7.6 and 7.2 heatwave days annually - up 162% and 136%, respectively, from 1986–2005.
The average annual monetised value of heat-related mortality among people aged over 65 reached $3.8 billion during 2021–2025, equivalent to approximately 216,000 average annual incomes and 495% higher than in 2000–2004.
Deaths linked to human-caused PM₂.₅ air pollution rose 40% in Bangladesh between 2016 and 2023, with fossil fuels contributing to 37.5% of these deaths in 2023.
Household air pollution was separately associated with 77,500 deaths that year, down from 90,700 in 2016. The monetised value of premature mortality due to air pollution reached $77.6 billion - equivalent to 16.4% of GDP.
Yet Bangladesh’s energy system became 9.9% more carbon-intensive between 2016 and 2023, while net fossil fuel subsidies reached $5.3 billion in 2024; equivalent to 52.9% of the national health budget.
Md. Ziaul Haque, additional director general of the Department of Environment (DoE), said the Lancet Countdown 2026 report provides important evidence on climate-related health risks, particularly for vulnerable communities.
He said Bangladesh must translate its NDC and National Adaptation Plan commitments into action. The report’s estimate of 239,000 deaths from human-caused particulate air pollution highlights the urgent need to reduce pollution and fossil fuel use.
Dr Atiq Rahman, executive director of the Centre for Advanced Studies (CSD), said climate change and health are directly linked. Rising temperatures are severely affecting working people, while mothers and children are increasingly vulnerable to climate-related health risks.
“Unfortunately, we have delayed taking appropriate action. Had we acted earlier, we could have better protected people from these impacts,” he said.
Bangladesh reported that its national meteorological and hydrological services provide climate information to the health sector, which can support preparedness for and responses to climate-related risks.
The country also referenced climate–health links in its 2025 United Nations General Debate statement for the second consecutive year.
Health-relevant content appeared in two of the five climate-related legislative documents assessed that year.
Globally, health adaptation needs quantified by 48 developing countries amount to at least $3.3 billion annually, yet only $1.1 billion was committed in 2024; around one-third of those stated needs. Finance and human resources were identified as the leading barriers to implementing Health National Adaptation Plans.
Professor Marina Romanello, executive director of the Lancet Countdown, based at University College London, said climate-related health harms were growing faster than the global response, despite progress in clean energy and health-system preparedness.
Dr Ainun Nishat, emeritus professor at the Centre of Climate Change and Environmental Research, Brac University, stated that the Lancet Countdown provides an important evidence base, but our response must reflect local realities.
Many people have no choice but to work outdoors, even during extreme heat. If global temperatures continue to rise at the current rate, the average temperature could increase by 3.5°C by the end of this century.
“Our priority must now be to implement the Health National Adaptation Plan, with particular attention to food security, nutrition and vector-borne diseases.”
“Accurate, locally relevant data is essential to understanding the health impacts of climate change. Bangladesh is a small country, yet temperatures and health risks vary considerably across regions. We need evidence that reflects these differences and helps identify where action is most needed.”
“He stressed that reducing fossil fuel consumption is essential, while expanding renewable energy could help curb pollution. He also expressed concern over the coal mine, warning that the high sulphur content of coal could increase the risk of acid rain. Climate change is also accelerating the spread of infectious diseases, he said, adding that the lack of visible progress in Bangladesh in addressing these challenges is particularly concerning.”
Tahrim Ariba Chaudhury, global climate and health lead at GSCC, said climate-related health costs, including families’ out-of-pocket medical expenses, must be central to policy discussions at COP31.
She stressed the need to make renewable energy an attractive and profitable investment in Bangladesh to support a sustainable energy transition and protect public health.

item.title: PM asks all to stay alert to ensure factory operations, public safety
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday directed all concerned to remain alert to ensure the smooth operation of factories and industries and the safety of people's lives and property amid growing labor unrest.
Labor and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury disclosed the prime minister’s instructions while talking to reporters after a meeting with him at the Secretariat at night.
“The prime minister said factories and industries must operate properly and the lives and property of people must remain safe. He asked everyone to stay alert and take appropriate measures in this regard,” the minister said.
He said the meeting discussed the overall situation surrounding the ongoing movement by garment workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000 and the clashes between workers and police in Mirpur.
Ariful Haque, also the expatriates’ welfare and overseas employment minister, said they also discussed public security and ways to restore stability.
“Vested interests are conspiring to create instability ahead of December and destabilize the government. We discussed the issue and how to deal with those involved in such conspiracies,” he said.
The minister alleged that some people are using political parties and different organizations, including those linked to workers, to carry out conspiracies against the government.
“InshaAllah, we will deal with this politically,” he said.
The meeting began at 6pm at the Cabinet Division conference room at the Secretariat.
Prime Minister’s Political Adviser Nazrul Islam Khan, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, State Minister for Local Government Ariful Haque, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin and Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal’s Chief Coordinator Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas, MP, among others, attended the meeting.
In the wake of the unrest in the country's garment sector, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman sat in the emergency meeting to address the crisis.
Garment workers staged demonstrations and blocked roads in Dhaka, Ashulia and Gazipur on Sunday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, disrupting traffic and triggering clashes with police and vandalism.
At least 20 people, including four to five police personnel, were injured in sporadic clashes between police and RMG workers in the capital's Mirpur area during the demonstrations.

item.title: Dhaka to have 8 e-rickshaw zones with separate colours, no driving licences for now
item.description:
Dhaka will be divided into eight zones for the operation of battery-powered rickshaws, with separate colours assigned to vehicles in each zone, as the government moves to regulate their movement in urban areas.
However, e-rickshaw drivers will not be required to obtain driving licences immediately. Instead, they will initially receive identification cards, with the government planning to introduce a licensing system gradually after registration gets underway.
State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam announced the decisions at a press conference at the Secretariat on Sunday, outlining key provisions of the newly issued Three-Wheeled Slow-Speed Battery-Operated Rickshaw (E-Rickshaw) Operation Rules, 2026.
The state minister said the 13 city corporations across the country would be able to begin registration from Monday, urging existing drivers not to panic over the new regulations.
Dhaka North and Dhaka South city corporations will each be divided into four zones. E-rickshaws operating in each zone will have a distinct colour and vehicles registered for one zone will not be allowed to operate in another.
The number of e-rickshaws permitted in each zone will be determined through discussions between the respective city corporations and traffic departments.
Shahe Alam said the government would not immediately remove all e-rickshaws currently operating on the roads. Instead, authorities would register eligible vehicles in phases while gradually removing unauthorised ones.
Under the new rules, the initial registration fee for an e-rickshaw designed to carry two passengers will be Tk8,000, with an annual renewal fee of Tk4,000.
For vehicles designed to carry four passengers, the registration fee will be Tk10,000, while the annual renewal fee will be Tk5,000.
Owners will also have to pay Tk1,000 for a number plate. The initial registration fee will be paid once, while the renewal fee will be payable annually.
The state minister said there would be no fixed limit on the number of e-rickshaws that could initially be registered.
However, existing vehicles must be structurally modified to comply with designs approved by the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet) before receiving registration.
Each registered vehicle will receive a unique number plate with a QR code, which must be displayed prominently. The code will contain information about the registration number, owner, driver, registering city corporation and designated operating zone, according to the minister.
A single national identity card will be eligible for the registration of a maximum of five e-rickshaws across one or more city corporations.
Each vehicle will have an economic lifespan of 12 years from its registration date. Its registration and number plate must be cancelled after that period expires.
Although the new regulations provide for driver licensing, the government will not implement the requirement immediately, the state minister said.
He cited the administrative challenge of processing licence applications for hundreds of thousands of drivers at once.
“We should first start the registration process. Once it has progressed to some extent, we will issue a separate notification and move to driving licences,” Shahe Alam said.
In the meantime, vehicle owners will issue identification cards to their drivers. The government plans to bring drivers under a formal licensing system in phases.
Existing e-rickshaws will be eligible for registration after necessary structural modifications to meet Buet's prescribed technical standards and safety specifications.
They will also need fitness certificates countersigned by the relevant traffic department.
Asked whether Buet had the capacity to oversee structural modifications to hundreds of thousands of vehicles, the state minister said the university would not carry out the modifications itself.
Buet had provided the designs, he said, adding that manufacturers would modify the vehicles in accordance with those specifications after obtaining permission from the relevant city corporations.
Newly registered vehicles and those seeking renewal must also meet the prescribed technical and safety requirements and obtain fitness certificates.
No e-rickshaw will be permitted to operate without registration or the required renewal.
Under the regulations, e-rickshaws will have a maximum speed limit of 25 kilometres per hour. The limit will be reduced to 15kmph around schools, hospitals, religious institutions and crowded public places.
Each vehicle must be equipped with a speedometer or odometer, while passenger capacity will be limited to two or four people, depending on the vehicle's design, excluding the driver.
E-rickshaws will be prohibited from operating on national highways, expressways, elevated expressways, major bus routes, footpaths and roads designated as restricted by the authorities.
City corporations, in consultation with traffic departments, will designate parking areas.
Violations involving unregistered vehicles, excessive speed or passenger loads, unauthorised batteries, modifications to motors or vehicle structures without approval, and operation on prohibited roads will be subject to legal action.
Authorities may also take action against drivers for carrying commercial goods instead of passengers, violating traffic signals or fleeing after an accident.
The government will determine e-rickshaw fares after the registration process begins, the state minister said.
Vehicle owners' representatives, traffic departments and city corporations will jointly discuss and set fares on a per-kilometre basis, taking operating costs into account while ensuring that charges remain affordable for passengers.
Asked whether drivers would participate in the fare-setting discussions, Shahe Alam said the owners' representatives would be involved, but drivers would not have a role in determining fares.
Battery-charging facilities will also be brought under a regulatory framework.
According to the state minister, city corporations will approve or issue trade licences to charging stations capable of providing solar-powered charging facilities.
The government plans to encourage a combination of solar power and grid electricity at charging stations. Under a net-metering arrangement, facilities will be able to supply surplus solar-generated electricity to the grid during the day and use grid electricity to charge batteries at night.
Legal action will be taken against operators using unauthorised electricity connections for charging. City corporation magistrates will oversee enforcement, he said.
The rules also prohibit dumping or burning old or unusable batteries in open spaces, on land, in water bodies or in ordinary waste streams.
Battery sellers will be required to collect old batteries when selling new ones and send them to recycling facilities. Batteries cannot be broken down or smelted without clearance from the Department of Environment, the state minister said.
The state minister did not provide an estimate of the number of e-rickshaws currently operating in Dhaka or a specific deadline for completing the modification of existing vehicles.
He said the government would hold another briefing with journalists after a month to report on the number of vehicles registered, measures taken and plans to remove unauthorised e-rickshaws.
The rules will initially apply to the country's 13 city corporations. Extending the system to municipalities will require amendments to the relevant laws, after which separate regulations will be developed for other urban areas.
Reassuring existing drivers, Shahe Alam said: “For now, they can continue operating as they are. We will gradually register vehicles in compliance with the rules and take steps to remove illegal battery-powered e-rickshaws in phases.”

item.title: Dhaka’s bus franchise system begins amid unresolved questions
item.description:
Bus services under a franchise-based system have begun on seven routes in Dhaka, comprising six regular routes and one circular route, as part of the capital's long-delayed bus route rationalisation initiative.
However, the launch on Sunday has left several issues unresolved, including the absence of new buses, delays in repainting existing vehicles, route allocation disputes and questions over whether the new system can bring discipline to the city's chaotic public transport network.
The services have been introduced using existing buses rather than newly procured vehicles. Moreover, many of the buses scheduled to operate on the six routes were not on the roads on the opening day.
The Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA) plans to operate 831 buses under six companies as part of the latest phase of a broader initiative to reduce Dhaka's 98 existing bus routes to 32.
Under the new arrangement, each company will operate on designated routes, with separate colours and route numbers planned to make buses easier for passengers to identify.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed said the authorities could not repaint the buses before the launch due to time constraints.
Speaking at the inauguration ceremony at Manik Mia Avenue around 11:30 am on Sunday, he said previous attempts to reorganise Dhaka's bus routes had failed because of a lack of cooperation from transport owners, workers and other stakeholders, as well as bureaucratic complications.
He also proposed replacing the existing trip-based payment system for drivers and helpers with fixed monthly salaries, arguing that this would reduce unhealthy competition among drivers to complete more trips.
The programme was inaugurated by Shimul Biswas MP, chief coordinator of the Transport Owners and Workers Unity Council.
The six regular routes are Shibbari in Gazipur–Dhakeshwari Temple, Mirpur–Keraniganj, Ghatar Char–Demra, Ghatar Char–Kanchpur, Ghatar Char–Uttara and Tongi–Azimpur.
Meanwhile, an air-conditioned circular bus service has also started operating from Mirpur-1 through Kachukhet, Sainik Club, Jahangir Gate and Agargaon to Ansar Camp. The service is being operated by Trust Transport Services using 30 new AC buses.
Shimul Biswas said the authorities had decided to introduce separate colours for buses operating on each of the 32 routes, following examples from major cities in developed countries.
"This will not be just a photo session today followed by the service being discontinued later," he said.
He said restoring discipline to Dhaka's roads would benefit the majority, even if some people profited from the existing disorder.
Referring to traffic congestion and the widespread presence of battery-powered rickshaws and other vehicles, he said the resulting loss of working hours, time and money was affecting the country's economy.
He added that disorder on the roads also shaped foreign visitors' perceptions of Bangladesh.
DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed said six companies had been formed by bringing bus operators previously running under around 18 different banners under a single management structure.
He said that, among 25 planned circular routes within the city, five had initially been approved. One has now been launched using AC buses, while 27-seat minibuses have been ordered for the remaining four routes, which are expected to become operational within the next two months.
He added that the authorities were discussing fixed monthly salaries for transport workers with bus owners' and workers' associations. Separate colours, route numbers and digital destination boards would also be introduced on buses operating across the 32 routes.
The six routes were inaugurated despite unresolved issues surrounding the number of buses, vehicle fitness, repainting, route allocation and operational arrangements. This has raised questions over how successful the initiative will be in bringing discipline to Dhaka's chaotic public transport system.
DTCA Executive Director Mohammad Mashiur Rahman described the initiative as a final implementation rather than a pilot project, saying there would be no turning back.
He also called for legal action, through traffic police and executive magistrates, against those obstructing the initiative by deliberately parking buses on roads.
Despite plans to operate 831 buses across the six regular routes, a significant number were missing from the roads on the first day.
On route 17, connecting Mirpur and Babubazar Bridge, 133 buses were scheduled to operate under the Chiriakhana City Transport Company, formed by bringing Dishari, Tanzil and Metrolink services together.
However, only Dishari buses were seen operating on the route on Sunday, while buses from the other two operators were absent.
ASM Ahmed Khokon, president of the bus owners' association under Chiriakhana City Transport, told Dhaka Tribune that 60 Dishari buses had started operating on Sunday, while buses from Tanzil and Metrolink would join the service from Monday.
Visiting several of the newly launched routes, this correspondent also found that buses continued to stop frequently at locations other than designated bus stops, undermining one of the key objectives of the rationalisation initiative.
Khokon acknowledged the challenge, saying both passengers and transport operators had become accustomed to irregular practices.
"We have become accustomed to irregularities, and passengers have also become accustomed to them. As an owners' association, we are trying to ensure that buses stop only at designated stops. Everyone's cooperation is necessary," he said.
Dhrubo Alam, deputy transport planner at the DTCA, told Dhaka Tribune that around 70% of the planned 831 buses across the six routes had started operating on the opening day.
He said the buses would be repainted soon.
Although the authorities have proposed fixed monthly salaries for drivers, transport owners say the existing system cannot be changed overnight.
According to the owners' association, drivers have been working under a daily payment arrangement for around 40 years. Any transition to monthly salaries would therefore need to be gradual.
During the inauguration ceremony Bangladesh Road Transport Owners Association Secretary General Saiful Alam urged passengers to board and get off buses only at designated stops to help restore discipline on the roads.
Despite the launch of the new arrangement, passengers on the routes said their travel times remained largely unchanged.
Sabbir Rahman, a businessman who travelled from Demra Staff Quarter to Matsya Bhaban on route 19, operated by Ramzan Ali City Transport, told Dhaka Tribune that the journey took him around two hours.
"It used to take me two hours even before. I have not noticed any significant change," he said.
During the inauguration ceremony, Saiful Alam called for government assistance to facilitate the purchase of new buses, saying transport owners were willing to buy vehicles by making advance payments rather than seeking subsidies.
He said the owners' association would provide guarantees to support the purchases and that older buses would gradually be replaced with new ones.
The initiative to rationalise Dhaka's bus routes dates back to 2015, when then Dhaka North City Corporation mayor Annisul Huq introduced a plan to divide the city's routes into eight corridors, with buses operating in separate colours.
The initiative stalled following his death in 2017.
Later, under former mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, a new plan was taken to merge 246 bus companies into six franchise-based operators and reorganise 278 routes into 22 corridors.
In December 2021, Dhaka Nagar Paribahan was launched experimentally on the Ghatar Char–Signboard route. However, other operators could not be brought under the system, and the initiative eventually became inactive.
The programme stalled again following the July uprising. Although the interim government also attempted to introduce a franchise-based system, but it also failed.
After the BNP government assumed office, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held several meetings to restore discipline to Dhaka's public transport system. The latest launch marks a partial start of the franchise-based arrangement within the six-month timeframe.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Additional Secretary of the Urban Transport Wing of the Road Transport and Highways Division Anisur Rahman, Bangladesh Road Transport Authority Chairman Mohammad Habibur Rahman and Dhaka Road Transport Owners Association President MA Baten, among others. It was chaired by DTCA Executive Director Mohammad Mashiur Rahman.

item.title: PM sits with ministers over garment sector unrest
item.description:
In the wake of the unrest in the country's garment sector, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has sat in a meeting to address the crisis.
The meeting started at 6pm at the Bangladesh Secretariat with the participation of several ministers and others concerned.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, PM’s adviser and also PMO Spokesperson Mahdi Amin and Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal chief coordinator and transport leader Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas attended the meeting.
Garment workers staged demonstrations and blocked roads in Dhaka and Gazipur on Sunday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, disrupting traffic and triggering clashes with police and vandalism.
At least 20 people, including four to five police personnel, were injured in sporadic clashes between police and workers in the capital's Mirpur area as workers took to the streets to press for their demand.

item.title: TIB: Money and muscle power increasingly influence political parties
item.description:
The growing influence of money and muscle power in Bangladesh's political landscape is raising concerns over democratic practices within political parties, with a new study identifying gaps in internal democracy, financial transparency and accountability.
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) presented the findings in a report titled Institutional Governance of Political Parties in Bangladesh at a press conference in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, on Sunday.
The report found that political parties lack clear guidelines on financial management, income and expenditure records, auditing and accountability. It also identified a lack of effective mechanisms to prevent individuals involved in criminal activities from joining parties or securing important positions.
According to the study, 16 political parties do not regularly hold national conferences. Among them, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has not held a national conference in more than 10 years.
The parties also do not prepare annual budgets, with a large portion of their income and expenditure managed through program-based and informal processes.
The study found that the constitutions of 18 political parties do not specify minimum integrity and moral standards for membership. Nor do they contain effective provisions to prevent individuals involved in criminal activities from becoming members or holding important positions.
The report said political parties are increasingly seeking individuals with money and muscle power to finance party activities, meet expenses, establish dominance and control polling centers during elections.
At the same time, individuals who accumulate wealth through illegal means and possess muscle power seek political influence to secure protection and gain social standing.
Individuals involved in crimes such as extortion, human trafficking, smuggling, and arms and drug trading have also been found joining relatively influential political parties, the study said.
It further found that between 18% and 32% of candidates who contested the past 5 national parliamentary elections had at least 1 case filed against them over alleged involvement in various crimes.
TIB identified widespread shortcomings in the financial management of political parties, saying none of the parties studied had clear financial policies or procedures.
Their constitutions contain unclear provisions on income and expenditure, membership fees, donation acceptance, financial transactions, form fees, auditing and financial accountability.
The report also found that parties lack effective mechanisms to hold nominated candidates accountable for violating state regulations, including electoral codes of conduct.
Candidates have also concealed or provided incorrect and incomplete information in election affidavits about their assets, loans, business interests and foreign citizenship, it said.
Party constitutions also lack clear guidelines on candidates' election expenditure plans, sources of funds, expenditure monitoring and the submission of financial reports.
According to the study, candidates spent an average of 169.5% more than the prescribed expenditure limit in the 13th National Parliamentary Election, but political parties took no effective action over the violations.
TIB also found that parties rarely take visible action against allegations that their leaders and activists accumulate wealth through criminal activities, irregularities and corruption. In some cases, minor disciplinary measures are imposed to close the matter.
The study found shortcomings in political parties' disclosure of information. Of the 32 parties included in the research, 24 have websites, but only 16 are active.
Its overall findings point to extensive gaps in transparency, accountability, democratic practices, participation and inclusion in the institutional activities of political parties, alongside inadequate measures to prevent irregularities and corruption.
Although laws and regulations govern party registration and participation in national elections, the report identified the absence of a strong legal framework to ensure internal democracy, transparency and accountability in political financing.
It also said the existing legal framework does not fully align with international good practices.
Despite the substantial funds required to run political parties, much of their financial management depends on informal processes and individual arrangements. This creates significant discrepancies between officially disclosed income and expenditure and the actual financial situation, the report said.
The dominance of individual dependence and informal funding sources is also contributing to the development of individual- and family-centered politics within parties.
The study further identified the growing influence of black money, misuse of power, political criminalization and internal conflicts, particularly within influential political parties.
In many cases, political participation and party positions are increasingly becoming power-centered business models, it said.
Progress in women's political participation also remains limited, despite legal obligations and party commitments. The report said parties remain reluctant to ensure women's inclusion, with their presence in some party activities being largely nominal or symbolic.
Shortcomings in democratic practices, grassroots participation and the inclusion of female activists are further reinforcing single-person leadership, dynastic politics, authoritarianism, oligarchy and patriarchy within political parties, the study observed.
The study was conducted using qualitative methods, drawing on information from primary and secondary sources.
TIB contacted 42 political parties, including 37 registered and 5 unregistered parties, and received information from 32. The remaining 10 did not provide information despite repeated attempts to contact them.
The report also noted delays, non-cooperation and the submission of partial information by political parties and relevant stakeholders during data collection.
Information was collected in 2 phases: the first from June 2023 to February 2024 and the second from June 2025 to September 2026.
Speaking at the press conference, TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said political parties are among the most important institutions in a democratic system.
He said political parties had made significant contributions to Bangladesh's history and achievements, while also bearing responsibility for various challenges to democratic progress and good governance.
“Democracy cannot be properly implemented if good governance is not ensured within political parties, which are among the central institutions of the democratic system,” he said.
“We generally talk about reforms in various state institutions, but the issue of internal reforms within political parties is often overlooked. However, institutional good governance within political parties is extremely important for establishing democracy,” he added.
Iftekharuzzaman said the study considered the roles of political parties and people's expectations of them.
He said the research began in June 2023, but changes in the country's political context and challenges in obtaining cooperation from political parties during information collection prolonged the process of completing the report.

item.title: Titumir: Govt to implement reforms with five stakeholders to ensure sustainable LDC graduation
item.description:
The government has undertaken a comprehensive reform initiative involving five key stakeholders - the people, private sector, United Nations, development partners and multilateral development institutions - to ensure Bangladesh's sustainable graduation from the Least Developed Country (LDC) category.
The government does not want to treat the additional three years granted for LDC graduation preparation merely as an extension of time. Instead, it aims to utilise the period to implement structural reforms in the economy, enhance productivity, explore new markets and lay the foundation for long-term sustainable development.
Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir said this in an interview at the Bangladesh Secretariat on Sunday.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had set a vision of transforming Bangladesh into a global manufacturing hub and an export gateway. To achieve this goal, the government is working on a strategy to transform the country from "graduation to a trillion-dollar economy", while ensuring that the transformation remains sustainable.
Titumir said Bangladesh has the largest economy among the LDCs and, therefore, requires major reforms to diversify its economy, enhance competitiveness and increase productivity.
Explaining the rationale for the extended preparation period, the adviser said the government considers it an integral part of its broader economic strategy.
He identified three key considerations behind the decision: domestic economic vulnerabilities inherited from the previous administration, external pressures and economic uncertainties arising from the Middle East crisis, and the country's inadequate preparation to address these challenges.
"Taking these realities into consideration, the government has started working on the necessary measures. However, the government has supported LDC graduation from the very beginning," he said.
Regarding reform priorities, the Prime Minister's adviser said restoring discipline in the banking sector and ensuring adequate financing for investment are among the government's major objectives.
The government will also focus on strengthening energy security, exploring new investment markets and diversifying the country's export basket. It will pursue free trade agreements (FTAs) with different countries to mitigate the possible loss of trade preferences following LDC graduation.
Titumir said achieving these objectives would become easier through an effective compact with the private sector.
He said private sector representatives had been involved in every discussion on LDC graduation, adding that the initiative also forms part of the government's "Three Rs" strategy.
The adviser said the government had brought five stakeholders under the reform initiative: the people of Bangladesh, the private sector, the United Nations, development partners and multilateral development institutions.
He described the initiative as an unprecedented consensus-based partnership.
Highlighting the role of the United Nations, Titumir said a unanimously adopted proposal had mandated the UN system to provide all forms of support, including technical assistance, to Bangladesh's graduation preparations. The UN Resident Coordinator will lead the coordination of this assistance.
He said the International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank, Asian Development Bank (ADB), Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) had assured support for the priority reforms identified by the government.
Titumir added that the ongoing IMF programme and other reform initiatives were aligned with the government's broader reform agenda.
He said the reforms were being undertaken on the basis of the people's mandate, which was one of the distinctive features of the initiative.
"Never before have the people of the country been involved in reform initiatives in this manner," he said, adding that the participation of the five stakeholders would also help strengthen confidence among foreign investors.
The adviser identified energy security as a major prerequisite for sustainable industrialisation and investment.
He said the government planned to develop energy infrastructure centred on Matarbari while expanding the necessary facilities in other parts of the country.
To increase LNG import capacity, the government is working on establishing land-based LNG terminals alongside floating storage and regasification facilities.
The government is also prioritising increased solar power generation, reducing wastage and system losses in the energy supply chain, and diversifying sources of LNG imports.
Titumir said developing energy infrastructure beyond Matarbari, particularly in the southwestern region and other parts of the country, would create opportunities for geographically balanced industrialisation.
He said the government was also focusing on exploring new export destinations and pursuing FTAs or Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (CEPAs) with trading partners to address the potential reduction of duty-free and quota-free market access after LDC graduation.
The additional three years, he said, have created an important economic opportunity for Bangladesh.
Proper utilisation of the extended period could help strengthen the country's economic foundations through higher investment, new export markets, expanded production capacity and increased employment opportunities.
The period, therefore, represents not only an opportunity to prepare for LDC graduation but also a crucial window for Bangladesh's long-term economic transformation.

item.title: Editors' Council urges restraint after PM aide tears up Amar Desh copy
item.description:
The Editors' Council has called for restraint and mutual respect in expressing differences of opinion after Prime Minister's Political Assistant Rashed Khan was seen tearing up a copy of the daily newspaper Amar Desh in a video posted on his Facebook page on Saturday.
In a statement signed by Editors' Council President Nurul Kabir and General Secretary Dewan Hanif Mahmud, the council said disagreeing with news reports or editorial opinions was a democratic right.
However, it stressed the importance of maintaining responsibility, decency and mutual respect when expressing differences of opinion.
The council said that as the prime minister's political assistant and a person holding the rank of secretary, Rashed Khan was expected to demonstrate restraint and responsibility in his statements and conduct.
It also emphasized the importance of maintaining professional standards, objectivity, ethics and accountability in journalism.
The Editors' Council called on all concerned to refrain from provocative statements, threats and harassment, and to uphold media freedom and the safety of journalists.

item.title: Sajek gunfight continues for second day, panic grips area
item.description:
Clashes between the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (JSS-Santu Larma faction) and the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF-Prasit faction) over territorial dominance in Sajek, Baghaichhari upazila of Rangamati, continued for a second consecutive day on Sunday, triggering panic among local residents.
The groups exchanged gunfire intermittently for more than two hours.
The gunfight broke out around 3:15pm in Langal Mara, near Machalong, and at Moner Chura in the South Bhaibonchhara reserve forest area of Ward No 5 of Sajek Union. No casualties were reported initially.
A similar exchange of gunfire took place in the Kalabunia area of Sajek on Saturday.
Police, local residents and public representatives said the clashes erupted over territorial dominance, with the two groups exchanging fire in the areas from around 3:15pm until 5:30pm.
Porichoy Chakma, a member of Ward No 5 of Sajek Union, told Dhaka Tribune: “Gunfire broke out around 3:15pm at Moner Chura in the South Bhaibonchhara reserve forest area. As the area is remote and has no nearby settlements, no immediate reports of casualties were available.”
Heavy gunfire erupted between the JSS and UPDF in the Kalabunia area of Ward No 5 of Sajek Union from 1pm to 4pm on Saturday. According to a reliable source, two people, one from each group, were killed in the clash. However, no organisation has confirmed the reported deaths.
Sajek Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Toffazzal Hossain confirmed that clashes between the two groups had continued for a second consecutive day.
He told Dhaka Tribune: “We have received reports that the JSS and UPDF have been exchanging gunfire for more than two hours over territorial dominance in the Langal Mara and Moner Chura areas. No casualties have been reported so far. We are looking into the matter.”
Meanwhile, following two consecutive days of clashes between the rival regional groups in the remote areas of Sajek, law enforcement agencies have stepped up security measures to bring the situation under control. The gunfights have sparked panic among local residents, who have expressed concern over the escalating tension.
Separately, two organisations have announced a one-day suspension of their blockade on the Sajek road in Rangamati. However, transport workers have opposed the decision and called a counter-blockade, creating fresh uncertainty over road communications in the area.
Vehicle movement on the Dighinala-Sajek-Baghaichhari road has remained suspended since Sunday morning as drivers and transport workers demand higher wages and allowances. However, inter-district bus services between Rangamati and Khagrachhari and other routes remain operational.

item.title: BUET, DU, BMU websites among 15 top educational institutions at cyber risk
item.description:
Several websites of some of Bangladesh’s leading educational institutions, including Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), the University of Dhaka (DU) and Bangladesh Medical University (BMU), remain vulnerable to potential cyberattacks due to unpatched security flaws in outdated versions of the PHP programming language.
The list of affected websites includes those of at least 15 prominent educational institutions, raising concerns over the security of institutional systems and potentially sensitive information related to students, faculty members and academic activities.
According to data from the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Division, more than 1,000 public and private websites across the country were initially identified as potentially vulnerable due to PHP security flaws.
The latest available information, however, indicates that more than 100 websites remain at risk. Most of them belong to private organizations, although government agencies and IT companies are also among those affected.
Among the educational institutions identified are Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB), Bangladesh Agricultural University, Asian University for Women, National University and Sonargaon University.
Websites associated with Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Rajshahi University, the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST), and Sapporo Dental College and Hospital have also been included in the list.
The exposure has raised concerns because university websites and associated digital platforms may contain sensitive personal and institutional information.
Departmental websites, learning management systems, admission portals and online service platforms may store students’ personal details, registration records, academic information and other institutional data.
If attackers exploit the vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access, the confidentiality and integrity of such information could be compromised.
However, there is currently no confirmed information indicating that student data have been stolen or leaked from the identified websites.
Cybersecurity experts warn that running outdated or unsupported PHP versions can expose websites and servers to attacks, particularly when the systems are directly accessible through the internet.
Depending on the nature of the vulnerability and the server configuration, attackers may attempt to execute malicious code, gain unauthorized access to servers or take control of affected websites.
Internationally, the PHP security vulnerabilities have already triggered significant concern among cybersecurity professionals.
According to information shared by Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince, attempts to exploit the vulnerability reached several million within the first 10 hours after the issue became public.
Against this backdrop, Bangladesh's government cybersecurity agency, Bangladesh Government's e-Government Computer Incident Response Team (BGD e-GOV CIRT), issued security advisories urging public and private organizations to identify their use of PHP and take necessary protective measures.
The advisory covered government and private institutions, banks, telecommunications operators, critical information infrastructure, educational institutions and other organizations.
BGD e-GOV CIRT recommended prioritizing security updates for servers directly connected to the internet.
Where immediate updates are not possible, organizations have been advised to temporarily disable vulnerable services or restrict access while examining server logs for suspicious activities.
Institutions have also been urged to identify the PHP versions running on their websites and servers and take appropriate measures to address the vulnerabilities.
When contacted, ICT Division Secretary Md Mamunur Rashid Bhuiyan said the government was regularly alerting public and private organizations to emerging cybersecurity threats.
“Many organizations have already taken necessary measures and secured their systems after receiving the warnings. The ICT Division will also provide the necessary technical assistance to institutions that require support,” he said.
He added that instead of issuing separate warnings to individual public and private universities, the ICT Division would communicate the advisory through the University Grants Commission (UGC).
The initiative is intended to reduce the risk of information exposure involving students and other stakeholders while ensuring the security of university websites and servers.
With more than 100 websites reportedly remaining vulnerable, timely security updates, regular monitoring and stronger institutional cybersecurity measures are essential to prevent potential attacks and protect sensitive information.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir: Extended LDC graduation timeline a major diplomatic success
item.description:
Acting Foreign Minister Humaiun Kobir on Sunday said the decision to extend Bangladesh’s preparatory period for graduation from the least developed country (LDC) category by three years is a significant diplomatic success for the country.
“Extending the timeframe for LDC graduation is an important diplomatic success for Bangladesh. We achieved this success within just eight months of the formation of the government under the capable leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman,” he told UNB over the phone on Sunday.
He said they have been able to properly explain its necessity to the United Nations and the international community.
Kobir made the remarks ahead of his participation in the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), scheduled to be held in Antigua and Barbuda from November 1 to 4 as the acting foreign minister.
The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) has recently unanimously adopted a resolution granting Bangladesh a three-year extension of its preparatory period for graduation from the Least Developed Countries (LDC) category, extending the deadline to November 24, 2029.
The decision marks a significant diplomatic achievement for the current government, giving Bangladesh additional time to strengthen economic resilience, enhance export competitiveness and prepare for the eventual loss of LDC-specific trade preferences and international support measures, Bangladesh said on Friday.
Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Ambassador Irene Zubaida Khan said, “Bangladesh is graduating from the LDC category not because the international process calls for it, but because graduation is an aspiration of our people. It is a national imperative, and our government is firmly committed to achieving that goal.”
Following the formation of the new government, Bangladesh formally requested the extension on 18 February 2026, citing global economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, changing trade dynamics, energy and supply-chain risks, and domestic economic challenges.
The UN Committee for Development Policy (CDP) recommended favorable consideration of the request.
Subsequently, on July 21, the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) recommended that the General Assembly take a final decision.
To facilitate the negotiations, the government developed a three-year roadmap outlining measurable actions to ensure a smooth and sustainable transition.
The extension period will provide additional time to address structural vulnerabilities, diversify exports, improve infrastructure and logistics, and implement essential economic reforms.
The extension offers Bangladesh a crucial window to implement necessary reforms and build a more competitive, diversified and resilient economy ahead of its revised graduation date.

item.title: Dengue: Eight more die, 1,929 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Eight dengue patients died in the last 24 hours till 8:00 am today while 1,929 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 427 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 831 were in Dhaka Division, 92 in Mymensingh Division, 257 in Chittagong Division, 259 in Khulna Division, 185 in Rajshahi Division, 73 in Rangpur Division, 213 in Barisal Division and 19 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 136,929 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 130,388 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: Bangladesh Bank rolls out P2P Bangla QR payments
item.description:
In a significant leap toward achieving a fully cashless economy, Bangladesh Bank officially introduced Person-to-Person (P2P) fund transfers via the unified national standard "Bangla QR" starting Sunday, November 1.
Under the new directive, account holders across participating commercial banks, Mobile Financial Services (MFS), and Payment Service Providers (PSPs) can transfer money directly to another individual by scanning a Bangla QR code or uploading an image of a beneficiary’s QR code using their mobile banking apps.
The interoperable platform automatically identifies the destination account or wallet, eliminating the need for customers to remember or check recipient account details across different platforms.
Central bank officials highlighted that the interoperable P2P system enhances transaction security, accuracy, and convenience for everyday financial transfers nationwide.
The national implementation of P2P Bangla QR follows a series of regulatory rollouts and rapid transaction growth over recent months.
The timeline began with official administrative instructions directing all banks, MFS operators, and PSPs to integrate P2P Bangla QR functionality into their mobile applications by October 31, 2026, setting the stage for today's live launch.
This expansion builds upon dramatic transaction growth earlier in the year.
According to central bank statistics reported across media, Bangla QR adoption surged extensively through 2026, with average daily transactions climbing from roughly 100,000 (valued at over Tk28 crore) in June to approximately 350,000 transactions (valued at around Tk143.54 crore) by late September.
Ahead of the P2P launch, Bangladesh Bank introduced instant merchant payment settlements starting October 1, 2026, alongside reduced transaction costs and fee incentives for transfers up to Tk2,000.
Financial analysts noted that these coordinated regulatory shifts and the introduction of P2P QR payments are expected to foster white-label Cash-In/Cash-Out (CICO) agent models and streamline small-scale personal money transfers across the country.

item.title: Vegetable prices drop, keeps food inflation at bay
item.description:
While the prices of certain commodities are declining in the domestic market, the costs of several daily essentials continue to rise.
A drop in the prices of vegetables, alongside rice and wheat, has led to a slight improvement in food inflation.
However, prices for nutritious items such as eggs, potatoes, fish, meat, and milk remain elevated.
Coupled with high prices for fuel and import-dependent goods, this is driving up the cost of living for ordinary citizens.
According to a Bangladesh Bank report titled "Inflation Dynamics in Bangladesh: July–September 2026," average food inflation dropped to 7.13% in the first quarter of FY27, down from 8.68% in the previous quarter.
Over the same period, overall inflation decreased from 9.21% to 8.31%.
Despite the decline in food inflation, not all commodity prices have fallen.
Protein-rich foods, in particular, are seeing price increases, with these items accounting for over 51% of food inflation.
Even as food prices have eased somewhat, inflation in the fuel sector has risen.
Bangladesh Bank data shows that fuel sector inflation reached 17.4% in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, compared to 17% in the previous quarter.
Inflation for traditional fuels—such as firewood, agricultural waste, cow dung, and jute sticks—increased from 21.8% to 22.1%. Similarly, inflation for liquid fuels and lubricants rose from 13.8% to 14.7%.
The report notes that although fuel prices were hiked toward the end of September, their full impact was not yet entirely reflected in the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
Consequently, fuel sector inflation is expected to rise further in the future. Increased fuel prices could also exert upward pressure on transportation and production costs.
The contribution of import-dependent goods to domestic inflation is also on the rise.
According to Bangladesh Bank calculations, 27% of overall inflation in the first quarter of the current fiscal year stemmed from import-dependent food and non-food items, up from 24.9% in the previous quarter.
Conversely, the contribution of domestic products declined from 75.1% to 73%.
A report by the Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission (BTTC) highlights that tariffs and duties on import-dependent fruits—such as malta, apples, pears, and grapes—have been increased at various times, driving up their market prices.
Furthermore, rising prices of various commodities in global markets are spilling over into the domestic market.
Alongside everyday essentials, ordinary people are struggling to cope with the costs of house rent, transportation, and healthcare.
A recent survey by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) revealed that 47% of households in the country are forced to take on debt to manage household expenses.
Bangladesh Bank's report states that because the inflation rate has outpaced wage growth over the past two years, people's real incomes and purchasing power have eroded.
Although the gap between wage growth and inflation narrowed slightly in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, it began to widen again toward September, primarily driven by a slowdown in wage growth.
Overall, while the food inflation statistics show some positive movement, the overall market situation is far from comfortable.
The high prices of fuel, import-dependent goods, and protein-rich foods, combined with sluggish wage growth, continue to exert heavy pressure on the cost of living and purchasing power of ordinary citizens.

item.title: Lux presents ‘Cafe Umbrella’ premieres exclusively on iScreen
item.description:
Love stories are filled with sweet moments, emotional ups and downs, misunderstandings and a wide spectrum of emotions.
Exploring these diverse dynamics of relationships is ‘Lux Presents Cafe Umbrella’, a new web film written and directed by acclaimed filmmaker Shihab Shaheen.
The web film was available exclusively on iScreen, Channel i’s OTT platform, from October 29.
Produced by Impress Telefilm and presented by Lux, ‘Cafe Umbrella’ features four distinct love stories involving four couples.
Alongside the sweetness of romance, the film explores relationship struggles, emotional conflicts, misunderstandings and the many facets of human emotions through different narratives.
These individual stories eventually come together in a common storyline.
One of the key attractions of the web film is the acting debut of the top three contestants of Lux Superstar 2025—Bidushi Barnita, Nazah Nawar and Amina Islam.
